subfamily: Collins: a whisky sour lengthened with soda (Cocktail Codex p. 138, Tom Collins); the Ward Eight as a reader sent it to Fougner's column in 1934 (Imbibe! pdf 243-244)
glass: large, heavy, round-bowled beer glass (about 400 ml), one large piece of ice
_status: v1 (Tomás, round 4). Every ingredient comes from the reader's letter or from Fougner; the departures from the letter (the shake, the measures, the fixed grenadine, the sugar left out) are mine and owned (Wondrich calls the one pre-Prohibition recipe 'rather lackluster', pdf 243; unseen, so no claim of what changed from it). From the letter: the reader's bourbon, his mint instead of crème de menthe ('This is an improvement'), the half orange 'many prefer' instead of orange bitters, his plain water or seltzer (seltzer: my pick), his 'rather large piece of ice' and beer glass, his fruit (two half slices orange, piece of pineapple, cherries; fresh cherry on the safe side); the grenadine made of real pomegranate after Fougner's June 1936 column (Oxford pdf 947). His barspoon of sugar is dropped under his own 'regulated to taste': with it, sugar goes OUT (8.00). Shaken 5 s (Codex Collins; the reader built it, Wondrich shook it). Sweep: bourbon 40/43/45/46% all in range, 47% edge, 50.5% OUT (16.3; +15 ml soda -> 15.3 edge); lemon 25-30 in, 35 acid edge; orange 30-40 in, 22.5 abv edge; grenadine 15 in, 20 sugar edge, 10 OUT; soda 45-60 in; bourbon 60 acid edge. Rejected: 60/30/30/15/60 (11.5% OUT), 75/30/30/+4 g sugar/20/60 (8.72 OUT), 75/30/30/20/60 (40% bourbon 11.8 OUT). Veto-free.
